testName: IISER IAT - The d- & f-Block Elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Electronic Configurations of the d-Block Elements
questions.question: Palladium (Z=46) belongs to the 4d series of the periodic table and exhibits a highly anomalous electronic configuration. What is the correct ground-state electronic configuration of a neutral Palladium atom?
options: [Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰
[Kr] 4d⁸ 5s²
[Kr] 4d⁹ 5s¹
[Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s²
questions.explanation: Palladium (Z=46) belongs to Group 10. While expected to be [Kr] 4d⁸ 5s², both 5s electrons migrate to the 4d orbital to achieve a highly stable, completely filled d-subshell, resulting in[Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: The melting points of transition elements initially increase to a maximum near the middle of each series and then fall. Among all 3d, 4d, and 5d transition metals, which element possesses the highest absolute melting point, and what is the primary structural reason?
options: Tungsten (W); it possesses a maximum number of unpaired electrons participating in strong interatomic metallic bonding.
Chromium (Cr); its perfectly half-filled 3d orbitals provide a rigid and highly symmetrical lattice structure.
Manganese (Mn); it has an extremely complex crystal lattice structure that resists thermal degradation.
Osmium (Os); it has the highest density in the periodic table, correlating to immense metallic lattice energy.
questions.explanation: Melting points depend on metallic bonding strength, driven by unpaired (n-1)d electrons. Tungsten (5d series) has immense enthalpy of atomization and multiple unpaired electrons (5d⁴ 6s²), granting it the highest melting point of all metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: In quantitative redox titrations, acidified potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) is frequently used to estimate reducing agents. How many moles of acidified KMnO₄ are theoretically required to completely oxidize exactly 1 mole of ferrous oxalate (FeC₂O₄)?
options: 0.6 moles
0.4 moles
1.2 moles
1.5 moles
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ oxidizes to Fe³⁺ (1 electron lost). Oxalate (C₂O₄²⁻) oxidizes to 2CO₂ releasing 2 electrons. Total electrons lost per mole of FeC₂O₄ = 3. Since KMnO₄ gains 5 electrons in acidic medium, required moles = 3/5 = 0.6 mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: An aqueous solution containing a transition metal complex exhibits a experimentally determined spin-only magnetic moment of 3.87 BM. If the complex is an octahedral aquo complex of a 3d series element, which of the following pairs represents the possible central metal ions?
options: V²⁺ or Cr³⁺
Mn²⁺ or Fe³⁺
Co³⁺ or Ni²⁺
Ti³⁺ or Cu²⁺
questions.explanation: Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √(n(n+2)) = 3.87 BM implies n = 3 unpaired electrons. Both V²⁺ and Cr³⁺ possess a 3d³ configuration, meaning exactly 3 unpaired electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: When solid K₂Cr₂O₇ is heated with solid NaCl and concentrated H₂SO₄, a reddish-brown gas (X) is evolved. When X is passed through an aqueous NaOH solution, a yellow solution (Y) is formed. Acidifying Y with acetic acid and adding lead acetate gives a bright yellow precipitate (Z). Identify X, Y, and Z respectively.
options: X = CrO₂Cl₂, Y = Na₂CrO₄, Z = PbCrO₄
X = Cl₂, Y = NaOCl, Z = PbCl₂
X = CrCl₃, Y = Na₂Cr₂O₇, Z = PbCr₂O₇
X = CrO₂Cl₂, Y = Na₂Cr₂O₇, Z = PbCrO₄
questions.explanation: This is the Chromyl Chloride test. K₂Cr₂O₇ + NaCl + H₂SO₄ yields CrO₂Cl₂ (X, reddish-brown gas). Reacting with NaOH gives Na₂CrO₄ (Y, yellow solution). Adding lead acetate gives PbCrO₄ (Z, yellow ppt).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: In the quantitative volumetric analysis of an acidic solution of Mohr's salt using a standard KMnO₄ solution, why is dilute H₂SO₄ exclusively used to provide the acidic medium instead of dilute HCl or HNO₃?
options: HCl is oxidized to Cl₂ gas by KMnO₄, and HNO₃ acts as a competing oxidizing agent, both of which introduce severe volumetric errors.
H₂SO₄ uniquely acts as a catalyst for the reduction of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺.
HCl forms a permanent complex precipitate of MnCl₂, rendering the endpoint invisible.
HNO₃ rapidly reduces KMnO₄ to MnO₂, masking the pale pink endpoint.
questions.explanation: HCl reacts with KMnO₄ and is oxidized to Cl₂ gas, skewing the titration reading. HNO₃ is a strong oxidizing agent that will independently oxidize the Mohr's salt, also invalidating the titration. H₂SO₄ is stable and non-interfering.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: The Lanthanoids
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of transition elements possess almost identical atomic radii entirely as a direct thermodynamic consequence of the Lanthanoid Contraction?
options: Zr and Hf
Ti and Zr
Y and La
Nb and V
questions.explanation: The Lanthanoid Contraction heavily counteracts the expected radius increase from the 4d to 5d series. Zirconium (Zr, 4d) and Hafnium (Hf, 5d) are in the same group and end up with nearly identical atomic radii (~160 pm and ~159 pm respectively).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: The Lanthanoids
questions.question: Arrange the following lanthanoid hydroxides in the strictly decreasing order of their basic strength in an aqueous medium: La(OH)₃, Eu(OH)₃, Lu(OH)₃, Ce(OH)₃.
options: La(OH)₃ > Ce(OH)₃ > Eu(OH)₃ > Lu(OH)₃
Lu(OH)₃ > Eu(OH)₃ > Ce(OH)₃ > La(OH)₃
La(OH)₃ > Eu(OH)₃ > Ce(OH)₃ > Lu(OH)₃
Ce(OH)₃ > La(OH)₃ > Eu(OH)₃ > Lu(OH)₃
questions.explanation: Due to Lanthanoid Contraction, the size of Ln³⁺ ions continuously decreases from La to Lu. A smaller ionic radius increases the covalent character of the Ln-OH bond (Fajan's rule). Increased covalency makes releasing OH⁻ harder, so basicity strictly decreases from La(OH)₃ to Lu(OH)₃.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: The Actinoids
questions.question: Comparing the chemistry of Actinoids to Lanthanoids, Actinoids are known to exhibit a much larger number of variable oxidation states. What is the fundamental quantum-mechanical reason for this specific characteristic?
options: The energy gap between the 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals in actinoids is significantly smaller than the gap between the 4f, 5d, and 6s orbitals in lanthanoids.
Actinoids possess a much higher effective nuclear charge (Z_eff) which uniformly stabilizes multiple oxidation states.
The 5f orbitals are deeply buried within the atom and heavily shielded compared to the outer-reaching 4f orbitals.
Actinoids are predominantly highly radioactive, providing internal thermal energy required to permanently excite electrons to higher states.
questions.explanation: The closely matched comparable energies of the 5f, 6d, and 7s subshells allow electrons from all these levels to participate in bonding, giving actinoids a vast array of stable oxidation states compared to lanthanoids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question:
PASSAGE: The standard electrode potentials (E°_M²⁺/M and E°_M³⁺/M²⁺) of transition metals provide profound insight into the thermodynamic stability of their oxidation states in aqueous solutions. The E°_M²⁺/M values for the 3d series elements generally become less negative across the period, with notable anomalies at Mn and Zn.

Based on the passage and general 3d series trends, why does Copper (Cu) exhibit a positive standard reduction potential (E°_Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V), making it the only metal in the 3d series incapable of liberating H₂ gas from dilute acids?
options: The sum of its enthalpy of atomization (sublimation) and ionization enthalpies is exceptionally high, and its hydration enthalpy is insufficient to balance this massive energy requirement.
Copper has a completely filled 3d subshell in its elemental state, causing massive resistance to first ionization.
Copper possesses the highest absolute hydration enthalpy in the 3d series, which reverses the sign of the electrode potential.
The exchange energy of the 3d¹⁰ configuration strictly restricts its dissolution in acidic media.
questions.explanation: The positive E° value of Cu arises because the sum of ionization enthalpies and atomization enthalpy is very high, and the hydration enthalpy is insufficient to compensate. Additionally, the stability of d¹⁰ configuration in Cu and Cu⁺ contributes to this behavior.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: Given the passage states that E°_Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ is highly negative (-0.41 V) while E°_Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ is highly positive (+1.57 V), which of the following chemical behaviors is correctly deduced in an aqueous solution?
options: Cr²⁺ is a strong reducing agent that readily oxidizes to Cr³⁺, while Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidizing agent that eagerly reduces to Mn²⁺.
Cr²⁺ is a strong oxidizing agent, whereas Mn²⁺ is a strong reducing agent.
Both Cr³⁺ and Mn³⁺ are thermodynamically stable and totally resist any redox changes.
Mn³⁺ spontaneously disproportionates in water to directly yield MnO₄⁻ and elemental Mn.
questions.explanation: A negative E° means the oxidized (+3) state is preferred. Thus, Cr²⁺ oxidizes easily to Cr³⁺ (reducing agent). A positive E° means the reduced (+2) state is strongly preferred. Thus, Mn³⁺ reduces to Mn²⁺ (oxidizing agent).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: Which of the following thermodynamic components is the primary reason the E°_Zn²⁺/Zn value (-0.76 V) is significantly more negative than expected from the general progressing trend of the 3d series?
options: The anomalously high sublimation energy of solid Zinc metal.
The complete removal of the 4s electrons leaves a highly stable, completely filled 3d¹⁰ core in the Zn²⁺ ion, providing an extra thermodynamic driving force for its oxidation.
The unusually high hydration enthalpy of the Zn²⁺ ion compared to adjacent Cu²⁺.
Zinc possesses the absolute highest second ionization energy in the entire 3d series.
questions.explanation: Formation of Zn²⁺ results in a stable d¹⁰ configuration, which favors oxidation. Additionally, relatively lower hydration enthalpy and weaker metallic bonding contribute to the more negative reduction potential.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: Potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄) is stable only in strongly alkaline media. When the green-colored aqueous solution of K₂MnO₄ is acidified, it immediately undergoes a disproportionation reaction to yield a purple solution and a dark brown precipitate. Identify the exact oxidation states of Manganese in the two resulting products.
options: +7 and +4
+7 and +2
+6 and +4
+3 and +2
questions.explanation: In acidic media, manganate (+6) disproportionates to permanganate (MnO₄⁻, purple, +7) and manganese dioxide (MnO₂, dark brown ppt, +4). The reaction is 3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Applications of d- and f-Block Elements
questions.question:
Transition metals and their compounds are extensively utilized as industrial catalysts due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states. Match the following transition metal catalysts to their correct industrial process:
(I) V₂O₅
(II) TiCl₄ + Al(CH₃)₃
(III) Fe (finely divided)
(IV) PdCl₂
options: (I) Contact Process, (II) Ziegler-Natta Polymerization, (III) Haber Process, (IV) Wacker Process
(I) Haber Process, (II) Contact Process, (III) Wacker Process, (IV) Ziegler-Natta Polymerization
(I) Wacker Process, (II) Haber Process, (III) Contact Process, (IV) Ziegler-Natta Polymerization
(I) Contact Process, (II) Wacker Process, (III) Haber Process, (IV) Ziegler-Natta Polymerization
questions.explanation: PdCl₂ is used in the Wacker process, where ethene is oxidized to ethanal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: Transition metals readily form interstitial compounds with small non-metals like H, C, and N trapped within their crystal lattices. Which of the following statements regarding the physical and chemical characteristics of these interstitial compounds is INCORRECT?
options: They exhibit significantly higher melting points than their respective pure parent metals.
They are chemically highly reactive due to the violent disruption of the pure metallic lattice.
They perfectly retain their metallic conductivity despite the presence of non-metal atoms in the voids.
They are extremely hard, with some specific transition metal borides approaching the hardness of diamond.
questions.explanation: Interstitial compounds are notably chemically inert, not highly reactive. The trapping of small non-metal atoms stabilizes the lattice, locking the planes in place, which increases hardness and melting points while destroying reactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: The Lanthanoids
questions.question: Mischmetal is a well-known, highly significant alloy of lanthanoid metals used extensively in the production of magnesium-based alloys and pyrophoric lighter flints. What is the approximate standard compositional breakdown of Mischmetal?
options: ~95% Lanthanoid metals, ~5% Iron, and traces of S, C, Ca, and Al.
~50% Cerium, ~50% Actinoids, and traces of Iron.
~95% Iron, ~5% Lanthanoid metals, and traces of Carbon.
~70% Magnesium, ~25% Lanthanoid metals, and ~5% Iron.
questions.explanation: Mischmetal is a classic lanthanoid alloy primarily consisting of approximately 95% Lanthanoid metals (mostly Cerium and Lanthanum), ~5% Iron, and trace impurities like S, C, Ca, and Al.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: In a highly acidic medium, KMnO₄ quantitatively oxidizes hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) to O₂ gas. If exactly 20 mL of a 0.1 M KMnO₄ solution completely reacts with an unknown volume of a 0.5 M H₂O₂ solution, what is the volume of the H₂O₂ solution used, and what is the equivalent weight of KMnO₄ in this specific reaction? (Given Molecular Weight of KMnO₄ = 158 g/mol)
options: 25 mL; 158 g/eq
questions.explanation: In acidic medium: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5H₂O₂ + 6H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5O₂ + 8H₂O. Thus, 2 moles KMnO₄ react with 5 moles H₂O₂. Using normality method gives V₂ = 10 mL. Equivalent weight of KMnO₄ = 158/5 = 31.6 g/eq.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: The Actinoids
questions.question: The "Actinoid Contraction" observed across the 5f series from Actinium to Lawrencium is measurably greater from element to element than the "Lanthanoid Contraction" observed across the 4f series. What primarily accounts for this amplified contraction effect?
options: The 5f electrons penetrate the inner core much more effectively than 4f electrons, increasing the direct nuclear pull.
The 5f electrons provide significantly poorer shielding from the continuously increasing nuclear charge compared to the 4f electrons.
The actinoid elements possess much higher atomic masses, causing extreme relativistic contractions of the s-orbitals.
The actinoids exhibit much higher oxidation states, which inherently shrinks their ionic radii more drastically.
questions.explanation: 5f orbitals provide poor shielding of nuclear charge, similar to 4f orbitals, but due to their complex radial distribution, shielding remains ineffective. This results in a stronger effective nuclear charge and greater contraction across the actinoid series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: General Properties of the Transition Elements
questions.question: Which of the following transition metal ions is entirely colorless in an aqueous solution due to the complete absence of d-d electron transitions?
options: Ti³⁺
Sc³⁺
V³⁺
Fe²⁺
questions.explanation: Color in transition metals originates primarily from d-d transitions. Scandium (Z=21) has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹ 4s². The Sc³⁺ ion loses all 3 valence electrons, leaving a 3d⁰ configuration. With no d-electrons, d-d transitions cannot occur, rendering it completely colorless.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.question: Chromate (CrO₄²⁻) and dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) ions are directly interconvertible in an aqueous solution depending entirely on the pH. Which of the following statements accurately describes their structures and pH-dependent equilibrium?
options: In highly acidic media (pH < 4), the yellow chromate ion dominates; the dichromate structure features a Cr–O–Cr bond angle of exactly 180°.
In highly basic media (pH > 7), the yellow chromate ion dominates; both chromate and dichromate feature a tetrahedral geometry around their respective Chromium atoms.
In highly acidic media (pH < 4), the orange dichromate ion dominates; the chromate structure features a square planar geometry.
In highly basic media (pH > 7), the orange dichromate ion dominates; the dichromate structure features a Cr–O–Cr bond angle of exactly 109.5°.
questions.explanation: Chromate (yellow) is stable in basic media, while dichromate (orange) is stable in acidic media. Structurally, both ions feature Chromium at the center of a tetrahedron of oxygen atoms. In dichromate, two tetrahedrons share an oxygen corner with a Cr–O–Cr angle of 126°.
